builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ActionGuard: Tool Call Authorization under Poisoned Skills
summary: Replaces safeguards that expose the reviewer to raw, potentially poisoned skill text with an execution-boundary Reviewer that authorizes each tool call using only the trusted user request, a balanced skill profile, recent tool calls, and local script contents, enforced fail-closed at the before-tool-call hook. Costs one additional LLM review call per tool invocation, adding latency and API expense, plus integration with an interception layer such as OpenClaw. Can fail if the Reviewer model misclassifies contextual injections, if the balanced skill profile omits legitimate task requirements causing false denials, or if attacks bypass the interception point entirely.
rationale: The guardrail runs as a pre-execution check with a single reviewer model, which fits one-GPU or API-only infrastructure and addresses a concrete production risk for any agent consuming third-party skills.
technique: Execution-boundary tool-call authorization against skill injection

claims.statement: Replaces safeguards that expose the reviewer to raw, potentially poisoned skill text with an execution-boundary Reviewer that authorizes each tool call using only the trusted user request, a balanced skill profile, recent tool calls, and local script contents, enforced fail-closed at the before-tool-call hook. Costs one additional LLM review call per tool invocation, adding latency and API expense, plus integration with an interception layer such as OpenClaw. Can fail if the Reviewer model misclassifies contextual injections, if the balanced skill profile omits legitimate task requirements causing false denials, or if attacks bypass the interception point entirely.

Reduced Attack Success Rate by 35.54–46.11% relative to existing safeguards (Dynamic Guardian, SkillGuard) and by 70.44% relative to no safeguard, while maintaining high benign-task completion, across 319 injections and five Reviewer models.
